items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: Usually like from the center of the state, you know, J.R. Monterose, Sal Nistico, the Mangione brothers...

ctx.x: You know there’s been, I guess we can consider you an Upstate New York guy, all the way from Albany to Buffalo, and there’s been really quite a long list of great jazz players to come out of —

Usually like from the center of the state, you know, J.R. Monterose, Sal Nistico, the Mangione brothers and then on the west side we had like Don Menza and Sam Noto. But I think I’m the only one from Albany.
You know I just noticed a weird thing as you went through those names is they all end in a vowel.
